session_title: Combining web search MCPs into unified orchestrator

message.text:
Hello, Can you please look up at the project, and make the following: The acceptance criteria that the TL requested are the following:

```
criterios de aceptación: 

- al menos tres recursos 
- Al menos 5 herramientas, dos de ellas, deben de consumir una API de internet (Ambas deben ser servicios en la nube diferentes)
- Al menos 2 prompts para consumir las API de internet 
- Debe estar desplegado para poderlo consumir en cualquier cliente 
- No debe de pedir autenticación 
- Debe de enviar el link al correo (angelo.gaviria@riwi.io) junto con al menos, una skill para agentes
- Se debe enviar junto con la documentación y el código del proyecto. 

Recuerden que todo lo que hagamos, debe de seguir los lineamientos del anterior proyecto de la carpeta "coding-assistance"
```

Now, this MCP alone doesn't fulfill them, and it won't make sense for it do it alone when it's using the free DucKDucKGo instant search Api.
Therefore, I'll combine it with my other web-search MCPs, that way:
There's a single MCP that offers the entity web search, profound web search and agentic web search from the API keys
It has the prompts that allow the AI to identify which one to use, how many credits are available, which one to use and how much to actually look up.
And create the skill set (Taking some of the tavila skills) to create a set of considerations and methods of use to determine which is the API that should be used when.

So, the other MCPs are these ones: 

https://github.com/SrLampi1001/tavily-search-mcp

https://github.com/SrLampi1001/fireclaw-search-mcp

Now, the objective will be to first, forward the MCP using the VS Code tunnel forwarding (no auth), and if it works and everything is loaded, then we are good.
Currently neither of the MCPs have custom skills, so that will need to be developed and implemented into the MCP.

I'll say that only combining the three MCPs into a single Free Web Search that "orchestrates" free search across multiple APIs (Brave is not included because of it's terms of service) would get up pretty close to the acceptance criteria.

So, what do you say? Can you do it?
Would you create a plan or develop it right away using sub agents by dividing tasks and using Spec Driven Development? 

Also, consider to follow an architecture, in this case, microservices would be the best since the other API calls shouldn't depend on each other, but honestly I don't think we have time for that, so modular monolith with layered architecture for each API is, or is there a better one?
And for design pattern, following [this catalog](https://refactoring.guru/design-patterns/catalog), I think that the ones we would use the most are command and strategy (kind of?), but I'm not so sure, so I would like your help to define them.

So, how is it? what do you think about it? I guess you would need first to explore the repositories.
Gladly, they all share the same FastMCP and MCP 2026 tech stack, so I don't think it'll be that hard to combine.
